LESSON: READING 11.2.2 COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.2: Reading 11.2.2 Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 11.2.2 Comprehension, part of Strand 11 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why do we need to summarise what we read?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 11.2.2 Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: The learner’s ability to speak engagingly is improved as they retell a story, poem or conversation using their

own words.

• Creativity and imagination: The learner’s ability to make connections is enhanced as they talk about their own experiences in relation to the

story.

Values:
Responsibility: Self-drive is heightened as the learner takes initiative to get clues from the story read to answer indirect questions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Social-economic issues (Safety and security): The learner gains and uses information on safety during playtime and games.

Link to other Learning Areas

The learner uses the comprehension skills when reading texts in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

● Print textbooks in appropriate font size and colour contrast

● Braille books

● Digital devices with assistive technology,

● Charts, flash cards or braille cards,

● Pictures or picture description
